title: Fractal: Joint Multi-Level Sparse Pattern Tuning of Accuracy and Performance for DNN Pruning
problem: Sparse DNN models from pruning exhibit irregular memory access and computation patterns that limit performance gains. Current approaches use single-level structured sparse patterns, failing to explore the full design space for optimal sparsity exploitation.
motivation: Model pruning is essential for efficient DNN deployment, but realizing its benefits requires better sparse pattern designs that overcome irregular memory access overheads.
method: Fractal interprets sparse pattern design as computation-skipping after multi-level hierarchical tiling of tensor operations, expanding the design space beyond single-level patterns. The system introduces PatternIR, a high-level intermediate representation that uniformly expresses diverse multi-level sparse patterns. Fractal's auto-tuning engine identifies optimal patterns for each DNN, then compiles PatternIR to low-level compiler IRs using insights from dense operator optimization for code generation.
key_novelty: Multi-level sparse tiling framework that unifies sparse pattern design as hierarchical computation-skipping, enabling joint exploration of accuracy-performance trade-offs across multiple tiling levels.
contributions: Multi-level sparse tiling perspective that expands design space beyond single-level patterns
PatternIR high-level intermediate representation for expressing and composing diverse sparse patterns
Fractal auto-tuning system for identifying optimal multi-level sparse patterns
Demonstrated speedups of 3.16× on CUDA and 2.52× on TensorCore under 75% sparsity

metrics.speedup: 3.16× on CUDA Core, 2.52× on TensorCore at 75% sparsity
metrics.accuracy: minimal degradation compared to prior sparse libraries
